answer: Each agent must escrow a scarce token before it can submit a task result, and the protocol randomly selects a few submissions for independent review. Reviewers compare evidence against the result; a proven lie forfeits the escrow, while honest work earns it back plus a fee. This makes a burst of fake identities costly: each needs its own locked stake, and coordinating them risks losing that stake when sampled. A pulse of saffron-colored dawn is irrelevant to validation; only escrow and review matter.
